# aarch64-study

> A web-first AArch64 SoC simulator for teaching operating-system internals.
> The simulator core is written in Rust, compiled to WebAssembly, and
> rendered in a React UI; every fetch / page-table walk / exception is
> observable in the browser. Each released version (`v0.1` … `v0.16`) adds
> exactly one architectural concept on top of the previous one, so reading
> the diff is the lesson.

Live demo: <https://labs.golia.jp/aarch64/>
License: MIT

## Documentation

- [README.md](README.md): trilingual project README (EN / 中文 / 日本語)
  with feature list, quick-start, roadmap, and repo layout.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): version-by-version history of every
  architectural concept introduced.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): dev model (git-flow on `develop`),
  local setup, style guide.
- [LICENSE](LICENSE): MIT license text.

## Source layout

- `crates/aarch64-sim/` — Rust simulator. `src/lib.rs` contains the entire
  CPU, MMU, AIC, Block device, demo program, and tests. `pkg/` is the
  wasm-pack output that the web side imports.
- `src/views/cpu.tsx` — main interactive view. Composes panels and owns
  the `<Cpu>` instance, refresh loop, and event derivation.
- `src/views/about.tsx` — roadmap + repo layout + commands.
- `src/components/system-diagram.tsx` — the SoC pin-out SVG schematic
  (two cores, 4-lane bus, peripherals, RAM grid).
- `src/sim/types.ts` — every domain interface (CoreState, AicState, …)
  shared by the React side; mirrors the Rust types exposed via
  wasm-bindgen.
- `src/sim/format.ts` — formatting + parsing helpers (fmtHex32/64,
  parseHex, parseCoreSlot, inferTaskLabel) and constants
  (REG_LABELS, MEMORY_VIEW_BYTES, RUN_BURST, TASK_*_ENTRY, IRQ_NAMES).
- `src/index.css` — global styles. Roboto Flex for UI text, Roboto Mono
  for numeric / hex / register columns. GDS theme tokens drive colour.
- `src/main.tsx` / `src/app.tsx` — router + layout shell.

## How a release is shaped

Each release introduces exactly one architectural concept that the user
can see in the browser. The shape is enforced by the changelog: if the
diff doesn't fit a one-liner, the concept needs to be split.

## Build & test

- `bun install` — install web deps + the local `aarch64-sim` crate.
- `bun run build:sim` — wasm-pack the Rust simulator. After this, run
  `rm -rf node_modules/aarch64-sim && bun install` so the new WASM is
  picked up by Vite (see `feedback_wasm_pkg_reinstall.md` in the user's
  notes).
- `bun run dev` — Vite dev server on `http://127.0.0.1:32030`.
- `bun run test:sim` — `cargo test` the Rust simulator (15 tests).
- `bun run test` — Vitest for the React side.
- `bun run check` — `tsc --noEmit && eslint src/ && prettier --check src/`.
- `bun run build` — production bundle into `./dist`.
- `bun run deploy` — build then `rsync` `dist/` to
  `t01:/apps/labs/aarch64/` (the production target behind
  <https://labs.golia.jp/aarch64/>).

## Conventions worth knowing

- The repo uses GDS (`@goliapkg/gds`) — the design system supplies `Card`,
  `Badge`, `Button`, theme tokens (`bg-surface`, `bg-bg-secondary`,
  `bg-bg-tertiary`, `text-fg`, `palette-X`, …), and Tailwind 4 wiring.
  Avoid hand-picking colour shades; use the tokens so light and dark
  themes both render cleanly.
- Numeric / hex / register columns are monospace (Roboto Mono via the
  `mono-data` helper). Plain UI text uses Roboto Flex with `tabular-nums`
  on.
- Animations must depict real simulator events. No ambient sci-fi.
- Tasks are pinned per core: core 0 runs task A (silent WFI sleeper),
  core 1 runs task B (the disk printer). Auto-run pauses the moment all
  cores are halted or WFI'd; pressing Run again auto-resets.
